To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CSR activities can be evaluated using a multi-dimensional approach that integrates financial and non-finical dimensions and perspectives, (2) the evaluation of CSR activities can be realized by considering stakeholder perception, (3) the stakeholder perception is influenced by the sustainability dimension and the perspective, and (4) the CSR activities can be assessed using the 2-tuples linguistic variables.
the CSR assessment is a multidimensional problem and that the stakeholder perception plays an important role in this assessment.

1) a company can be perceived as socially responsible or irresponsible depending of the considered dimension; 2) a company can have a different level of social responsibility for each dimension and perspective; 3) stakeholders can be classified according to their level of social responsibility perception.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new methodology for assessing CSR activities that is able to integrate financial and non-finatural sustainability dimensions, strategic perspectives and stakeholders' perception.
the development of an integrated CSR assessment model that allows the analysis of the company's social commitment from a stakeholder perspective.
the development of a multidimensional model to assess CSR activities and to measure stakeholder perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if a tree falls in a forest and no one hears it, then it does not produce any benefits for the company.
a company has a good CSR performance if it has high scores in all the dimensions of all the BSC perspectives.
, yes, a tree falling in the forest makes a sound, but only if it is perceived by someone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the context of CSR assessment, the stakeholder perception of a company is a key issue.
we provide a framework to measure CSR performance and to assess the social behavior of companies, considering different stakeholder perceptions and the multidimensionality of CSR.
the stakeholder perception of the CSR behavior of a company is a multidimensional issue, where the same company can appear as responsible or irresponsible at the same time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSR activities are not only important for the company, but they are also a source of competitive advantage for the company.
the stakeholder perception of CSR activities is a complex and multidimensional concept that can be assessed by means of a multidimensional approach.

CSR assessment is an important and challenging issue, and that the multidimensional approach proposed in this paper can be a useful tool for CSR managers and practitioners to better understand the impact of their social initiatives and the way stakeholders perceive the company's social performance.
